note: Zero-base round: options produced without sight of the current portfolio, then compared against the measured ETA. The proposal passed scripts/check-blind.mjs, so no name of ours appears in it.
route: chatgpt-ask.yml with danger-full-access; the account cannot read our private repos (measured 404), so it is blind to the portfolio while still able to research

options.why: borrows the plugin directory's existing search traffic; free version funnels to a paid Pro

refuted.claim_tested: first yen within 7-21 days, borrowing the WordPress plugin directory's search traffic
refuted.finding: The complaint is real and sourced — a weekly production cap shared across several products, resetting automatically — with three independent posts (WordPress.org support thread, r/Wordpress 2020-10-05, r/woocommerce 2020-02-24), and WooCommerce core does not provide it. But it is already occupied: Order Limit for WooCommerce ships the free version at 800+ active installs (4.2, 13 reviews, updated 2 months ago) and puts the store-wide weekly cap with automatic reset in its Pro at USD 49/year, and WPC Shared Stock (50+ installs, updated 7 days ago) already covers the shared-stock half. Monetisation is real and confirmed with sources (Order Limit Pro USD 49/yr; Independent Analytics Pro USD 49-199/yr, licence keys). What could not be found is any case of first yen reached on new directory traffic alone: the one same-day sale on record (Independent Analytics) launched to an existing user base and an announcement post, and the counter-example (Gato GraphQL) took about 2.5 months.
refuted.verdict: does not meet the 7-21 day claim as stated
refuted.not_refuted: that WordPress plugins can be sold, or that this complaint exists. Only this candidate's speed from a standing start with no list.

options.why: CI can publish and update it; a concrete time-saver reaches the English-speaking developer market directly

refuted.claim_tested: first yen within 3-14 days, borrowing Marketplace search traffic
refuted.finding: The recurring complaint the estimate rested on — approval fatigue in agent extensions — is already solved by VS Code itself (chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove, per-command allow/deny and a management UI) and by at least three free extensions. Those competitors sit at 95-1,472 installs, so the search traffic being borrowed is thin. Paid VS Code extensions do exist and were confirmed with sources (DV Quick Run, $19/mo via Lemon Squeezy licence keys; VSCode Maestro MCP, Gumroad one-off), so monetisation is real — but no case of first yen within 14 days was found.
refuted.verdict: does not meet the 3-14 day claim as stated
refuted.not_refuted: that VS Code extensions can be sold at all. Only this candidate's speed.

options.why: CI turns public data into a normalised, diffable feed people pay monthly for

refuted.claim_tested: first yen within 7-21 days from a maintained, normalised, diffable public-data feed sold by subscription
refuted.finding: The complaint is real and sourced — LiteLLM's price table is measurably incomplete (15 models missing, GitHub issue #22646, 2026-03-03), custom model prices do not reach cost calculation so spend reads $0.00 (#11975, 2025-06-23, re-reported 2026-03-11 and 2026-05-19), and per-provider dimensions such as cache read/write break a plain input/output table (#27191). But the space is occupied by a free incumbent, and not a thin one: Portkey Models is a free, auth-free API covering 2,000+ models across 40+ providers with normalised pricing including cache, image, video and search dimensions, used by 200+ companies for cost calculation on 400B tokens/day. It already solves most of the complaint the estimate rested on. No case was found of a normalised LLM-pricing feed converting free users to paid at all. The nearest first-yen example in an adjacent data API is Canopy API at about 12 days (public 2023-01-24, first organic paying customer 2023-02-05) — and that launch was an Indie Hackers post recruiting users with a discount offer, with any pre-existing readership unverified.
refuted.verdict: does not meet the 7-21 day claim as stated
refuted.not_refuted: that maintained data feeds can be sold. Only this candidate's speed from a standing start with no audience — and note nobody has yet shown paid demand for this particular feed at all, which is weaker than the other two, where monetisation was confirmed.

options.why: package search and README funnel to a commercial licence
captures validator/converter/generator searches with a free tool and sells the full version

the only route in the evidence that reaches a buyer without an audience and without recurring human posting: many individually findable pages, each carrying something computed rather than templated, so a third party can discover and refer one
options.added_because: the round contained five build acts and no distribution act, while every refutation landed on distribution. This is the missing class, not a sixth instance of the same one.
options.estimate_deliberately_absent: No days-to-first-yen is recorded. The other five carried numbers produced by the same model in the same round, and three of the three checked were refuted on exactly those numbers. Writing one here would reproduce the error this option exists to correct.
options.must_face_the_same_gauntlet: This was proposed from inside the loop, not blind, so it is more prone to motivated reasoning than the five it joins. It gets the same outside survey the others got, and its speed claim is refutable on the same terms.
options.known_failure_mode: Mass-generated pages that are templated with nothing computed per page read as content farming. The youtube repository already carries this lesson from platform policy: templated bulk output is judged unmonetisable regardless of volume. Per-page substance is a requirement, not a quality preference.

refuted.claim_tested: many individually findable pages, each carrying something computed rather than templated, reach a first buyer from zero audience with no recurring human posting, because a third party can discover and refer one
refuted.finding: No case was found with the full causal chain and both calendar dates. The nearest fast case (PredictionJobs, first $100 within 10 days) is the one this candidate was modelled on, and its own author attributes the sale to a large X account's post, not to search: there is no evidence the referrer found a specific page through search, and the pages were combinatorial templates rather than computed. Three counter-examples hit the candidate directly. Causal mass-published ~1,800 low-originality pages and took a Google manual action: organic traffic -99.52% (307,158 -> 1,485) over 2023-08 to 2024-08. Datanyze is the closest counter-example, because it had exactly what this candidate proposes — genuine per-entity data on each page — and still lost 95.46% of organic traffic, with over 80% of the loss concentrated in the two programmatic directories; the pages stayed HTTP 200 and indexed and were re-ranked down anyway. Stripe Fee Auditor tested the computed-value premise on its own: three months, 4,230 search impressions, 5 clicks, 2 real users, ¥0 — and Hacker News sent more real users in three hours than three months of search did. Google's own position matches: scaled content abuse (2024-03-05) covers mass low-originality pages whether generated or hand-written, and Search Essentials states outright that meeting the requirements does not guarantee crawl, index or display, and lists telling relevant communities as a basic step.
refuted.verdict: falls as a route to first yen from zero audience without recurring posting
refuted.not_refuted: that many search surfaces can work as a long-term acquisition play, and that per-page substance matters. What was refuted is this candidate's role: a route that reaches a FIRST buyer unattended. Note the survey answered the sub-question too — no case supports 'one computed value per page is enough'. The near-successes carried a page that could be acted on by itself (BuiltWith's technology list, IPinfo's IP metadata, Tunebat's key/BPM), and even those cannot be attributed to search for the first sale.
refuted.what_it_leaves: Four candidates have now been refuted by outside evidence and every one of them failed on the same term. In each near-success the first buyer arrived through a third party with reach posting about the thing — an X account, Hacker News, Product Hunt, Stack Overflow answers — and never through discovery working unattended. distribution_answer already elected route 2 (findable surfaces) over route 1 (post where the buyers already gather) not on evidence but on our own constraint that recurring owner actions are excluded; it said so plainly. This survey removes the evidence route 2 was resting on, so what remains is a constraint with no surviving route under it. That is a decision for a lap to take deliberately, not a gap to fill by proposing a sixth build candidate.

options.owner_actions: 1 initial + several hours of replies the same day, per attempt, not recurring
options.why: the one route in the evidence where a first buyer actually arrived from something we could do: a single honest post into the specific community the buyers are in, with the poster answering replies that day
options.added_because: route 1 was excluded on the ground that it needs repeated posting. The evidence in the same block describes a single post. See distribution_answer.route_1_exclusion_corrected. Route 2 was chosen over it and has since been refuted by 2026-08-09.h, so the constraint that did the excluding now has no surviving route under it.
options.estimate_deliberately_absent: No days-to-first-yen. Every number in this round was produced the same way and four of the four checked were refuted on exactly those numbers. Writing one here would repeat the error.
options.blocked_on: there is nothing to post about yet. This route reaches buyers for something that exists; it does not create it. Whether any of the 28 existing artifacts qualifies has never been examined.
options.must_face_the_same_gauntlet: This was proposed from inside the loop, like findable_surface_at_scale, and that one fell. It gets the same outside survey, aimed at breaking it: how often a single honest post into a buyer community produced a first sale, and what the accounts that tried it and failed had in common.
options.known_failure_mode: posting widely, or posting promotionally, produced one to six months at zero on record. The one case that worked posted about the outcome and the product's limits honestly, in one relevant community, and answered comments for hours.

ranked_last_by_blind_model.note: The blind model placed audience-zero content accumulation last without being told this is what we currently do. Independent agreement with the measured 0.023% conversion.

structural_insight: Every fast option borrows an existing marketplace's search demand instead of building an audience. The slow ones all start from zero attention. That is the axis, not the medium.
verdict_reason: Measured incumbent idle ETA is infinite on every channel. These are estimates rather than measurements, but any finite path beats infinity, and the capability they need (writing and shipping software) is the one thing this operation has demonstrated repeatedly.
caution: The month-count figures are the model's estimates, not observations. Treat first-yen as the falsifiable claim and measure it; do not carry the month figures forward as if measured.
outcome_note: Two of the five options have now been checked against the outside world, and both failed — vscode_extension_pro on 3-14 days, wordpress_plugin_pro on 7-21. Neither was refuted on whether the product can be sold; both were refuted on speed, and both for the same reason. The remaining three rest on the same kind of estimate and are unchecked.

premise_under_strain.premise: structural_insight above: the fast options are fast because they borrow an existing marketplace's search demand instead of building an audience.
premise_under_strain.status: three of five checked, all three refuted on speed. The discriminating survey this block asked for was run and is recorded in distribution_answer: the missing term is distribution, and the round contained no option that supplied one.
premise_under_strain.what_three_surveys_found: Refutation is no longer about marketplaces. vscode_extension_pro and wordpress_plugin_pro borrow marketplace search demand; maintained_data_or_api does not borrow any marketplace at all, and was picked precisely because it tests a different axis. All three came back the same way: the complaint was real and sourced, and the speed claim had no case behind it. In every one of them the only fast first-yen example on record launched into an audience that already existed — Independent Analytics to its own user base, Canopy API via an Indie Hackers post recruiting users with a discount. Two of three also found a free incumbent already serving the exact complaint (free VS Code extensions plus the editor itself; Order Limit for WooCommerce at 800+ installs; Portkey Models at 2,000+ models, free and auth-free).
premise_under_strain.what_this_says_instead: The estimates price building the product and treat reaching a buyer as free. That is the error they share, and it does not depend on where the demand comes from. 'Borrowed marketplace demand' was one guess at why the estimates were wrong; the evidence says the missing term is distribution, on both marketplace and non-marketplace candidates alike.
premise_under_strain.implication_if_it_holds: Days-to-first-yen for any candidate that starts with zero audience is dominated by how a first buyer is reached, not by what is built. If that is right, the two unrefuted options inherit the same defect — their estimates were produced the same way, by the same model, in the same round — and surveying them one at a time will keep returning the same verdict at one survey per lap.
premise_under_strain.next_test_that_would_actually_discrimina: Not another candidate. The question that separates the options is which of them comes with a way to reach a first buyer that does not require an audience we do not have. A survey aimed at candidates will keep answering 'the product is real, the speed is not'. Nobody has yet asked for cases of first yen reached with no pre-existing list, sorted by how the buyer was reached — which is the axis every refutation has landed on.
premise_under_strain.do_not_rediscover: The next zero-base round must be told: three of its five options were checked against outside evidence and all three failed on time-to-first-yen, for want of distribution rather than product. A round allowed to re-propose 'build X, the marketplace brings buyers' will spend itself re-deriving this.

distribution_answer.question_it_closes: premise_under_strain.next_test_that_would_actually_discriminate — cases of first yen with no pre-existing list, sorted by how the buyer was reached.
distribution_answer.finding: No case satisfied every condition at once (verifiably no audience AND both calendar dates confirmed). What the survey could establish is which routes carried a buyer at all. Two did: (1) a single honest post inside the community where the buyers already gather — one case sold the next morning off ~31k views and a dozen site visits; (2) long-tail searchable pages that a third party discovered and referred — PredictionJobs took $100 in about 10 days when a large account found its pages unprompted.
distribution_answer.what_was_shown_not_to_work: Publishing and waiting, with no route to a buyer. Product Hunt, general social posting, broad community posting and small-volume cold email each produced 1-6 months at zero on record. The strongest counter-example is Krumzi: about 1,200 signups and still no revenue, because the free users were not the payers. Signup count is not a proxy for reaching a buyer.
distribution_answer.why_this_settles_the_ranking: Every option in this round is a build act. None carries a distribution act. The portfolio has the identical defect measured in reality: 28 published artifacts, no route to a buyer, zero yen in eight months. That is the refuted pattern executed 28 times, so the refutations are not about the wrong marketplace being chosen.
distribution_answer.route_1_is_excluded_for_us_and_why: Reaching buyers by posting where they gather requires an account and repeated human posting. Recurring owner operations are excluded by design (the owner may not read instructions at all), and automating the posting gets the account banned, which destroys the asset it depends on. It is excluded on our constraints, not on its evidence — which is the stronger of the two.
distribution_answer.route_2_is_the_one_that_survives: Long-tail findable pages are the only evidence-carrying route that runs with zero recurring owner actions: generation, publication and measurement are all things this operation already does unattended.
distribution_answer.honest_weakness: Neither route has a case with both calendar dates confirmed, and route 2's one concrete case had a founder with a prior exit, so 'no audience' is unproven there. This is the least-unsupported route, not a demonstrated one.
distribution_answer.it_reprices_the_weekly_owner_action: The itch.io game page is itself a route-2 surface on a marketplace that has its own search. The recommended weekly action does not change. Its success test does: it is judged on whether anyone finds and refers the page, not on the page existing.

reprices_candidates.because: distribution_answer elected route 2 — long-tail findable pages a third party can discover and refer — as the only evidence-carrying route that runs with zero recurring owner actions. The itch.io page is a route-2 surface on a marketplace with its own search, so the action does not change but what counts as success does.
reprices_candidates.success_test: someone who was not told about the page finds it and refers it, or arrives from itch's own search or browse. Measured from state/itch.json views and from any referral that can be traced, not from the page's existence.
reprices_candidates.not_success: the page exists and is well made. That is the pattern the portfolio already ran 28 times: 28 published artifacts, no route to a buyer, ¥0 in eight months. Publishing and waiting was checked against outside evidence and produced one to six months at zero every time, and signup counts do not substitute — about 1,200 accounts and still no revenue in the clearest case on record.

route_1_exclusion_corrected.what_it_says: route 1 requires an account and REPEATED human posting, so it is excluded by the no-recurring-owner-actions constraint.
route_1_exclusion_corrected.why_that_ground_does_not_hold: The same block's own finding, two fields above, describes route 1 as 'a single honest post inside the community where the buyers already gather — one case sold the next morning'. Single, not repeated. Checked against the source rather than the summary: codex/outbox/2026-08-09.g.md records one post to a relevant subreddit, about 31,000 impressions, a dozen or so site visits, one purchase the next morning. codex/outbox/2026-08-09.h.md adds an independent instance of the same shape — Hacker News sent more real users in three hours than three months of search did. Neither case is recurring posting. The exclusion rules out a cost that the evidence for this route does not contain.
route_1_exclusion_corrected.what_the_honest_cost_actually_is: One post, plus several hours of a human answering comments the same day, on an account with enough standing in that community to post at all. That is a real cost and it is larger than the web-form action the plan's one-action-a-week budget assumes. It is not, however, a recurring cost, and the constraint that excluded it was about recurring costs.
route_1_exclusion_corrected.what_survives_of_the_exclusion: Automating the posting to avoid the human hours would destroy the account it depends on — that part stands and is not being reversed. So the route needs a human present for a few hours, once, per attempt.
route_1_exclusion_corrected.what_is_still_weak_about_the_route: g.md called its one route-1 case a single self-report with the product name, launch date and purchase record withheld, and rated the evidence weak. The same survey found broad or low-effort community posting produced one to six months at zero. The distinction the evidence draws is between an honest post into the specific community that has the buyers, with the poster present for the replies, and posting widely and waiting. Only the first has a case behind it, and only one.
route_1_exclusion_corrected.what_it_does_not_supply: Something to post about. Route 1 is a way of reaching buyers for a thing that exists and is worth their attention; it does not produce the thing. The portfolio's 28 artifacts were never checked for whether any of them is worth an honest post to a community that has buyers in it. Nobody has looked, which is different from having looked and found nothing.
